7.region_notes_beginner: In the Ozark Uplands and Delta Lowlands, sow cucumbers directly in the garden once the soil warms in April, for an early-summer harvest. heat_pause.basis_seasoned: Summer is a heat exclusion for fava beans, not a frost gap. Fava beans are a cool-season legume that grows best around 60 to 65°F and sets pods poorly once daytime temperatures climb past about 75 to 80°F, so a crop caught by summer heat drops its blossoms, forms few pods, and declines as rust and black bean aphids build up. The fall-sown crop is harvested well ahead of the heat, the bed then rests through the hottest months, and the calendar leaves summer out.
